findings.title: Authorization failure throws plain Error → 500 instead of a tRPC error
findings.body: When the credential does not exist or belongs to another user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC turns non-`TRPCError` throws into `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (HTTP 500) and reports them as unexpected server errors (noise in Sentry/logs), while the client only sees a generic failure. This should be `throw new TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN" | "NOT_FOUND", message: ... })` so the status code and client handling are correct.

findings.title: CalendarCacheRepository instantiated directly, bypassing the calendar-cache feature gate
findings.body: The handler does `new CalendarCacheRepository()` instead of going through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which is the factory that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the `calendar-cache` feature is disabled. As a result every `connectedCalendars` query now issues an extra `calendarCache.groupBy` query (this endpoint is called on the installed-apps and event-type calendar screens), and the UI will advertise "Cache Status"/"Delete cached data" for deployments or users where calendar cache is turned off. Use the existing factory so the feature flag is respected and the mock short-circuits the DB call.

findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The disconnect mutation invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`, but `deleteCacheMutation` only calls the optional `onSuccess?.()` callback (the `onChanged` prop, which is undefined in several call sites of `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`). Since `cacheUpdatedAt` comes from that query and `connectedCalendars` is configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, after a successful deletion the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated" timestamp and the now-meaningless "Delete cached data" entry until a full page reload. Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` to the mutation's onSuccess/onSettled.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to en-US formatting
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` formats the cache timestamp with US date order and 12-hour clock for every user, ignoring the user's locale (available via `useLocale()`) and their 12/24h `timeFormat` preference. Non-US users will see a date like `7/15/25, 4:06 PM`, which is confusing/ambiguous. Pass the active locale (and ideally the user's time format) instead of a literal.

findings.title: Cache status/delete is unavailable for Delegation Credential connections
findings.body: `hasCache` is derived from `cacheUpdatedAt`, which the handler resolves by matching `connectedCalendar.credentialId` against `CalendarCache.credentialId`. Delegation (domain-wide) connections surface in-memory credentials with negative ids, and their cache rows are looked up by `userId` (see `getCachedAvailability`'s `isInMemoryDelegationCredential` branch), so the map lookup never matches: for exactly the org users who most rely on calendar cache the dropdown is rendered as `null` (no cache status, no way to purge a bad cache). Either resolve cache status by userId for delegation credentials or document that the feature intentionally excludes them.

findings.title: Unused updateMany with empty data on every cache refresh
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is executed after every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` run (triggered by every Google webhook notification and by the watch cron) solely to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. It (a) relies on the implicit Prisma behaviour of emitting `SET updatedAt = now()` for an empty `data` object, which is fragile and non-obvious, (b) touches *all* selected calendars of the credential, including ones whose cache was not refreshed in this run, and (c) writes a value the PR itself states is not consumed anywhere (the UI reads `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache`). It also silently no-ops for in-memory delegation credentials whose id is negative. Remove it or make the intent explicit with an actual `updatedAt: new Date()` payload scoped to the refreshed calendars.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId types data as SelectedCalendarUpdateInput but calls updateMany
findings.body: `updateMany` accepts `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`, not `SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`. Because the parameter is typed with the latter, nested relation writes (e.g. `user: { connect: { id } }`, `eventType: { disconnect: true }`) type-check at the call site but are rejected by Prisma at runtime. Type the parameter as `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId that this module never reads
findings.body: `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` in the exported `UserWithCalendars` type were widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, but nothing in `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` (or the new cache-status code, which keys off `CalendarCache`) uses those fields. Every caller that builds this object from a narrower Prisma `select` (API v2 / platform-libraries call sites, onboarding handlers) now fails type-checking; the PR only updated one select (`UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession`). Either revert the type widening or update all the selects that feed this type.

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired cache is reported as present
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows for the credential with no `expiresAt` filter. Rows stay in the table after they expire (lookups filter on `expiresAt >= now()`), so the UI will show a "Last updated" timestamp and offer "Delete cached data" for a credential whose cache is no longer usable, giving a misleading picture of cache health. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or surface expiry separately).

findings.title: No tests for the new cache status/delete paths
findings.body: The PR adds a new mutation (`deleteCacheHandler`, including its ownership check), a new repository method (`CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), the credential→cache mapping in `connectedCalendarsHandler`, and a new UI component, with no unit or integration tests. At minimum the authorization branch of `deleteCacheHandler` (another user's credentialId must be rejected and must not delete rows) and the credentialId→updatedAt mapping should be covered, since a mapping bug would silently show one credential's cache state under another credential.

findings.title: Migration warning comment contradicts the actual SQL
findings.body: The header says "Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty." while the statement below actually adds the column with `DEFAULT NOW()`. A reviewer or operator reading the migration will believe it is a destructive/blocking change on a non-empty table. Remove or correct the stale auto-generated warning.

findings.title: dev:cron now runs an undeclared dependency via npx
findings.body: `dev:cron` was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`. `tsx` is not in this package's (or the repo's) dependencies, so `npx` will download it from the registry at run time — the script fails offline/in restricted CI and pulls an unpinned package version (supply-chain risk). `ts-node` is still listed in devDependencies but unused by this script. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it directly, or keep `ts-node`.

findings.title: Dev script uses macOS-only sed syntax and masks failures
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; on Linux (GNU sed) the empty argument is parsed as the input filename and the command fails with "can't read : No such file or directory", leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` un-updated. In addition `ENV_FILE="../.env"` only resolves correctly when the script is invoked from inside `scripts/`, and `cleanup()` always `exit 0`, so the "Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL" path returns a success exit status to the caller.
